subject: Cascade consent routing + DocuSign path for MSA + Order Form
messages:
From: AcmeCloud Legal <legal@acmecloud.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmecloud.com
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed redlines: Order Form + subprocessor cascade

Kimberly / Lauren —

Thanks for the call this morning. Attached are AcmeCloud's consolidated redlines to the Order Form and the MSA cascade clause. High level items for your team:

- We retained the standard subprocessors annex but added a requirement that any downstream subprocessor that handles customer data must accept the same DPA terms before onboarding.
- We added a flow-down notification window of 30 days for changes and a procurement right to object within 10 business days.
- We proposed a limited audit right scoped to SOC2 reports or equivalent rather than full audits.

Attachments: Acme_OrderForm-v3_redlines.pdf (pdf)

Request: please confirm whether Redwood can accept the 30-day notification + 10-day objection cadence; if not, propose alternate timing. Also confirm the order form signature path (can we route via DocuSign to the procurement contact once redlines are finalized?).

Best,
Sara Holden
Senior Counsel, AcmeCloud
legal@acmecloud.com
[Attachment: Acme_OrderForm-v3_redlines.pdf (pdf)]

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: AcmeCloud Legal <legal@acmecloud.com>, procurement@acmecloud.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed redlines: Order Form + subprocessor cascade

Acme team —

Thanks for sending. We're reviewing with procurement and security; quick notes upfront while we finish the internal review:

1) Notification window: 30 days for non-material subcontractor additions is tight for our ops but acceptable as long as emergency security patches (hotfix vendors) have a separate, immediate notification channel. Can we add "emergency security vendors excepted" language?

2) 10-business-day objection from procurement: reasonable, but we need a defined escalation path if an objection is raised (who signs off internally and whether the deal waits for resolution). Our suggested text: objections route to Procurement Lead + Security (Markus) and a 5-business-day internal escalation to VP Product for decisions on deal hold.

3) Audit scope: acceptable to accept SOC2 / ISO27001 summaries rather than on-site audits. Markus, please confirm the minimum evidence we should require in the Subproc_Matrix.

Attached two items from our side: Subproc_Matrix.xlsx (current vendor tiers and evidence levels) and a draft DPA amendment we would append if the cascade clause is accepted.

I will loop Sales (Priyom) to confirm the DocuSign routing and signature authority.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel — Contracts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Subproc_Matrix.xlsx]

Kimberly / Lauren —

Reviewed the matrix. Security position:

- Emergency vendors: agree to carve-out language for time-sensitive security vendors (monitoring, incident response). Suggest phrase: "vendors engaged for incident response or critical security patching to be notified as soon as practicable and documented within 5 business days."
- Evidence: for tier-1 subprocessors (handle customer content or keys) we require recent SOC2 Type II report plus secure configuration checklist; for tier-2 (support services) an ISO/attestation is acceptable. I'll add comments to Subproc_Matrix.xlsx.
- Audit: prefer consolidated attestations (SOC2/ISO) with right to request targeted questionnaires. Full on-site audits only for material incidents.

If Procurement objects within their 10-business window we will route to VP Product only if the objection would materially delay go-live; otherwise legal + security to resolve.

Markus
Director, Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: AcmeCloud Legal <legal@acmecloud.com>, procurement@acmecloud.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed redlines: Order Form + subprocessor cascade

Acme team —

Appreciate the quick turn. We are prepared to accept the cascade clause with the following set of final edits:

- Add explicit "emergency vendor" carve-out as Mark suggested; Redwood will expect documentation of emergency add-ons within 5 business days.
- Maintain 30-day non-material notification; procurement retains a 10-business-day objection window. If an objection is raised that would delay go-live, Procurement + Security escalate to VP Product; otherwise legal + security will triage.
- Audit scope limited to SOC2/ISO certifications + targeted questionnaires. On-site audits limited to post-incident investigations.

Next steps:
1) Acme to confirm acceptance of the three bullets above in an email reply.
2) Once confirmed, Acme to re-issue a clean Order Form PDF and route to procurement contact for signature via DocuSign (we will accept DocuSign envelope linked at: https://www.docusign.com/preview/ENVELOPE-29834).
3) Redwood will prepare the DPA amendment (attached: DPA_amendment_draft.docx) for insertion as an annex to the Order Form; if you prefer to redline the DPA directly please send edits back to me.

Please respond by EOD 5/7 to keep the current go-live commitment.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel — Contracts
Redwood Inference
[Attachments: Subproc_Matrix.xlsx; DPA_amendment_draft.docx]
